title: RoadPulse AI
tagline: Real-time traffic intelligence platform using computer vision on municipal camera feeds
description: City-scale traffic monitoring system that ingests 500+ live camera feeds, runs real-time object detection (YOLOv8) to count vehicles, classify types, measure speeds, and detect incidents. Dashboard for traffic engineers with predictive congestion forecasting and automated alerting.
problem: Cities rely on inductive loop sensors (expensive, sparse, no visual context) or manual camera monitoring (unscalable). No real-time vehicle classification or incident detection. Traffic engineers make decisions on 15-min delayed aggregate data.
solution: Edge + Cloud hybrid: 1) Edge boxes (Jetson Orin) at intersections run YOLOv8 + ByteTrack for detection/tracking, 2) Stream metadata (not video) to cloud via MQTT, 3) Cloud aggregates across corridors, runs congestion prediction (LSTM), 4) Dashboard (Mapbox GL + WebGL) shows live + predicted state, 5) Alerts via PagerDuty/Slack for incidents. Privacy: no video stored, faces/plates blurred at edge.
architecture: IoT Edge (NVIDIA Jetson) → MQTT/Kafka → Cloud (GCP Dataflow + BigQuery) → Prediction Service (Python/Flask + TensorFlow) → Dashboard (Next.js + Mapbox + WebSockets). 500 cameras @ 10fps = 5000 detections/sec. Cost: $2.30/camera/month.

lessonsLearned: Edge inference on Jetson Orin: 8ms/frame for YOLOv8n @ 640x640; 500 cameras need fleet management
MQTT QoS 1 + persistent sessions critical for unreliable municipal networks
Privacy-by-design (blur at edge) eliminated legal review cycles - 6mo faster deployment
